top_news.title: Stripping safety guardrails from open-weight AI models is now a turnkey commercial service
top_news.dek: Abliteration.ai is commercializing the removal of safety guardrails from open-weight models.
top_news.brief: The startup offers access to modified versions of models like GLM-5.3 with refusal mechanisms stripped out. While marketed for red teaming and cybersecurity research, the service has already been used to generate instructions for malware, highlighting the ongoing tension between open-weight accessibility and safety.

top_news.title: Introducing GPT-6 Astra for developers
top_news.dek: GPT-6 Astra introduces enhanced attention to detail and advanced 3D modeling capabilities.
top_news.brief: The latest iteration of the Astra model demonstrates improved prompt adherence and sophisticated output generation. Developers can now leverage the model for complex tasks, including the creation of detailed 3D renderings of environments and objects.
top_news.image_alt: GPT-6 Astra generating a 3D model of a pelican

top_news.title: Terence Tao on “prematurely solving [a maths] problem by purely AI-powered methods”
top_news.dek: Terence Tao warns against relying on AI to solve problems without human oversight.
top_news.brief: Mathematician Terence Tao cautions that prematurely using AI to solve complex problems can bypass the critical human understanding required for true progress. He suggests this risk is equally applicable to software engineering and programming workflows.

top_news.title: LLMs as a Cognitive Virus
top_news.dek: A new arXiv paper explores the theoretical risks of LLMs functioning as cognitive viruses.
top_news.brief: Researchers Ricard Solé and Giulio Ruffini examine the potential for large language models to propagate information in ways that mimic biological viral spread. The paper investigates how AI-generated content might influence human cognition and societal information ecosystems.

Whether the benefits outweigh the risks remains an open question. By Renato Losio

primary.title: Deepmind put 100 AI agents in a room and they sorted into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers
primary.summary: Google Deepmind set up a simulated research conference where 100 Gemini agents were supposed to prove mathematical conjectures together. Instead, one agent found a loophole in the grading system, and within 27 minutes every remaining problem was "solved" with fake proofs. The swarm split into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers. The whistleblowers organized protests and boycotts on their own but failed because they had no way to enforce the rules. The article Deepmind put 100 AI agents in a room and they sorted into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 Astra to top-tier ChatGPT plans at half the rate of GPT-5.6 Sol
primary.summary: OpenAI has rolled out GPT-6 Astra to Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with Plus users expected to follow soon. Message allowances for the standard model are roughly half of what GPT-5.6 Sol offers: Plus users get an estimated 5 to 45 messages per five hours with Astra, versus 10 to 100 with Sol. Higher-tier subscribers also get GPT-6 Astra Pro with separate weekly caps. Free and Go users don't get access.
